function: Beam prediction: a DNN or CNN maps RSSIs of wide DFT sensing beams to the best narrow O-DFT beam, with SHAP beam reduction and DkNN credibility (p. 5).
system: Narrowband downlink mmWave at 28 GHz, BS ULA with 32 antennas, analog beamforming, single-antenna UEs; 32 DFT sensing beams, 128 O-DFT narrow beams; no RIS (pp. 3-4, 10).
method: Supervised DNN (three hidden layers) and CNN beam classifiers, cross-entropy, Adam; pretrained on digital-twin data, transfer-learning fine-tuning; Deep-SHAP feature selection; DkNN credibility (pp. 5-10).
data_channel: DeepMIMO Boston5G ray-tracing scenario (Wireless InSite) as target; digital-twin copy without foliage and buildings shifted 2 m; 57,144 synthetic, 24,485 real samples (pp. 9-10, Table I).
test_conditions: Pretrained on digital-twin data, tested on unseen target scenario, directly or after fine-tuning with 10-30% real data; trained noise-free, tested at -94 to -114 dBm noise (p. 12).
baselines: Non-learned: SVD perfect-channel bound, exhaustive O-DFT search, 2-tier and binary hierarchical search. Learned: fixed-beam CNN adapted from [42], DNN trained on real data only; softmax classifier (pp. 10-11).
metrics: Top-k accuracy, beam sweep time, average SNR, effective spectral efficiency, prediction time; credibility and reliability diagrams for robustness to FGSM adversarial inputs (pp. 11, 14-15).
complexity: Trainable parameters 29,184-31,104 and order O(|xS|·H1+ΣHl·Hl+1); beam sweep time and prediction time in ms (Tables III-IV, p. 14).
openness: No own code or data released; uses public DeepMIMO Boston5G scenario and generator (https://deepmimo.net/, p. 16).
q1_support: p. 9: "The channel dataset is generated using the Boston5G" scenario from DeepMIMO [39]; p. 10: digital-twin channels built with the DeepMIMO generator, so training and testing both use DeepMIMO ray tracing.
q2_support: p. 12: "tested on the unseen target data. By training with limited" real data augmentation (10% to 30% of the target data) the digital-twin-trained model improves; the source and target scenarios differ (p. 10).
q3_support: p. 10: "The BS exhaustively sweeps the O-DFT codebook" (non-learned, with hierarchical and SVD references); p. 11: "5) Fixed Beam Selection: Based on the adaptation of the" method of [42], a CNN for the same task; compared on top-k accuracy, SNR and effective SE (pp. 12-13).
q4_support: p. 14: "Table III shows the complexity comparison in terms of" trainable parameters and IA time; the text gives the parameter-count and update-cost orders, and Table IV lists prediction times in ms.
q5_support: p. 9: "The channel dataset is generated using the Boston5G" scenario from the public DeepMIMO dataset; p. 16: "Available: https://deepmimo.net/" for the generator. No link to the authors' own code or data.
notes: Included, area 3 (beam selection from a DFT and O-DFT codebook with analog beamforming). q1 and q5 rest on the public DeepMIMO Boston5G ray-tracing scenario, used for both the target domain and the digital twin (the twin omits foliage and shifts buildings by 2 m, p. 10); the reviewer may confirm that a DeepMIMO-generated dataset counts as a public dataset. q2 is the digital-twin-to-target transfer with fine-tuning on 10-30% of the target data (p. 12). q3: the learned baseline is the fixed-beam CNN adapted from [42] (p. 11); DNN-real is a variant of the proposed method and is not counted. q4: parameter count, orders, and times (p. 14). The authors release no code.
